clue.text: It's contributed after whip-round, that's understood

indicators.note: the IT is added on behind the turned whip word, so it comes later in the answer
round asks for the whip word to be turned about, read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a cat (cat-o'-nine-tails) is a whip
It gives IT; the 's is part of the surface

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a coin dropped in after the office whip-round needs no saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip-round' looks like an office collection, but it is a whip (the cat-o'-nine-tails) plus the reversal signal 'round'; 'contributed after' is the placing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is implied without being spoken, which is to say understood.

clue.text: Adjust trousers, useless if split

parts.note: literally, hitching up the waistband, which won't help if the trousers have burst; idiomatically, cutting back spending

explanation.surface: Fixing one's trousers is pointless once they have torn.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means to economise; the surface takes it literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to spend less, literally to pull in the strap at one's waist.

clue.text: Pass on a couple of points in this

definitions.text: Pass on a couple of points in this

parts.words: Pass on a couple of points in this
parts.note: a punctuation mark made of two dots, and also the part of the gut through which food passes

explanation.surface: Advice to pass along a few points in a discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark is two dots, one above the other, and the same name is given to the large intestine.

clue.text: Lacking full cover as sound sleeper? Not so

parts.note: a top, in the saying 'sleep like a top'
less means not so much

explanation.surface: A heavy sleeper is told not to sleep without bedclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'sleep like a top' gives TOP for a sound sleeper. 'as' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A topless dancer is bare above the waist, without full covering.

clue.text: Cheap seats including rows in far from dirty condition?

indicators.note: including means the seats word holds the rows word within it

parts.note: the gods are the cheapest seats, high in a theatre's top gallery
rows are lines

explanation.surface: A theatre's cheap seats, rows and all, are in a spotless state.
explanation.walkthrough: THE GODS is British slang for a theatre's top gallery, where the cheapest seats are.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says cleanliness is next to piety, so a holy state is playfully called a far from dirty condition.

clue.text: Sound judge of fruit

indicators.note: Sound says we want a word that is pronounced like the judge word

parts.note: to gauge is to judge or estimate

explanation.surface: A good assessor of produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective (a sound judge), but it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gage is a plum, as in greengage.

clue.text: Steers dory at sea into other craft

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A man steers his little boat out to sea and into other vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: A dory is a small flat-bottomed boat, so 'other craft' fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Destroyers are fast warships, craft of another kind than a dory.

clue.text: Signs of power cuts — get home first

indicators.note: first puts the home word at the front

parts.note: in means at home
dices means cuts into cubes

explanation.surface: Power cuts mean everyone gets home early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power' is not electricity but the mathematical power, an exponent. 'get' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: In algebra, the small raised figures showing powers are called exponents or indices.

clue.text: Essential, as aluminium may be described?

explanation.surface: A chemist says what is key to aluminium.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means fundamental, and literally means being a chemical element, as aluminium is.

clue.text: Reluctance to buy, as necessaries last out

indicators.note: out says the letters of the two words are put out of order

explanation.surface: Shoppers resist buying while their essentials hold up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word, not fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoppers' unwillingness to be persuaded to buy is a marketing term.

clue.text: Festival opera thus brought back to islands

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
Pag is the opera-goer's short name for Pagliacci, as in 'Cav and Pag'

indicators.note: brought back says the word for thus is turned to read in the opposite direction

parts.note: so means thus

explanation.surface: A festival opera is staged again for an island audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns SO into OS. PAG is the stock short name for Leoncavallo's opera Pagliacci, usually paired with Cav (Cavalleria Rusticana).
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific archipelago off Ecuador famous for Darwin's finches is a group of islands.

clue.text: Live with wife in valley

indicators.note: in places the wife abbreviation within the valley word

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded valley

explanation.surface: Someone settles down with a spouse in a quiet valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside, to have one's home somewhere.

clue.text: Loving proposal

definitions.meaning: a formal offer, as a bid to do a job

explanation.surface: A two-word description of a romantic offer of marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender means affectionate, and a tender is a formal offer of a price for work.

clue.text: Mad solvers?

definitions.meaning: people who crack codes or puzzles

explanation.surface: Crossword fans are told they must be out of their minds.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is British slang for crazy, and code-breakers are said to crack codes.

clue.text: Chief villain's double, riddled with bullets?

indicators.note: riddled with means the double word is filled with the bullets word

parts.note: a ringer is a lookalike, a dead ringer
lead is bullets, as in 'pump full of lead'

explanation.surface: The gang boss's lookalike is shot full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is 'is' joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringleader is the head of a gang of wrongdoers.

clue.text: Producer of invention that one can't do without

definitions.meaning: the proverb calls this the mother of invention

explanation.surface: An inventor's indispensable source of ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb names need as the mother of invention, and a need is something indispensable.

clue.text: Go round endlessly with a friend? That's sweet

indicators.note: endlessly says the go-round word loses its final letter

parts.note: to cycle is to go round
mate means friend

explanation.surface: Going round and round with a pal is nice.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclamate is an artificial sweetener.

clue.text: Composer one runs into out East

indicators.note: runs into means the one word goes inside the rearranged letters
out says the letters of East are knocked out of their order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A composer bumps into someone while abroad in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges EAST into SATE, and 'runs into' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer, best known for the Gymnopedies.

clue.text: Metternich expected to hold a suitable position

indicators.note: to hold says the words Metternich expected keep the answer inside them

explanation.surface: The Austrian statesman Metternich expected to keep a fitting post.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a role or place exactly suited to someone.

clue.text: Vengeful daughter prepared claret, introducing drug

indicators.note: introducing means the rearranged wine takes the drug inside it
prepared means the letters of claret are made ready in a new form

parts.note: E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A vengeful daughter makes up some wine and spikes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' turns CLARET into ELCTRA, and 'introducing' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra in Greek myth avenged her father Agamemnon by having her mother killed.

clue.text: Soldier accepts a coarse but patriotic leader

indicators.note: accepts means the soldier word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
ribald means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: A soldier is crude but loyal to his country under his commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi was the Italian patriot who led the campaign for Italian unification.

clue.text: Showed resentment as brother wasted time

parts.note: idled means wasted time

explanation.surface: A sibling sulks over having loafed about.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to bristle with anger, like a horse throwing up its head.

clue.text: Bearing with exam as a standard for measuring one's rise

definitions.text: a standard for measuring one's rise

parts.note: SE (south-east) is a compass bearing
A level is the British school exam taken at about 18

explanation.surface: Someone's poise in an exam is the yardstick for their promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: A LEVEL is the advanced exam English pupils sit at the end of school. 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Heights such as a mountain's altitude are measured from the mean height of the oceans.

clue.text: I'm clinging tightly, as this might be mine

definitions.text: I'm clinging tightly, as this might be mine

parts.words: I'm clinging tightly, as this might be mine
parts.note: a shellfish famous for gripping rocks speaks, and its name is also given to a type of explosive mine stuck to ships' hulls

explanation.surface: A speaker hangs on hard, saying this could belong to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like the possessive, but it is the explosive device attached magnetically to a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The limpet is a shellfish that clings to rocks, and a limpet mine is one fixed to a target's hull.

clue.text: Meat spread on new dish

parts.note: pate is a paste of meat

explanation.surface: Meat paste is put on a fresh plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A paten is the plate for the communion bread.

clue.text: Face an animal that might be wild

definitions.text: an animal that might be wild
definitions.meaning: a cat, which may be a wild cat

explanation.surface: Facing an animal that could turn savage.
explanation.definitionFit: Puss is slang for the mouth or face, and a familiar name for a cat.

clue.text: Require means of execution to be rejected by court

indicators.note: by places the court abbreviation next to the turned word
to be rejected means the execution word is sent back, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the axe was a means of beheading

explanation.surface: Demanding that the executioner's weapon be refused by the judges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be rejected' turns AXE into EXA.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand or insist on something, as payment.

clue.text: Perhaps club pair's remarkable batting feat

definitions.meaning: in bridge, a holding of just two cards in a suit such as clubs
a double century, 200 runs, by one batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: A pair from the cricket club pull off an outstanding innings.
explanation.walkthrough: A TON is 100 runs in cricket, so a double ton is 200. In bridge, a suit of exactly two cards is so named.
explanation.definitionFit: The bridge term means a two-card suit, and a double century of runs is a rare achievement for a batsman.

clue.text: Reference book showing the end of many extinct reptiles

parts.note: taken as written
many dinosaur names end in -saurus, as tyrannosaurus and brontosaurus

explanation.surface: A book reveals how the dinosaurs died out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' is not the last letter: it is the shared ending of names like stegosaurus.
explanation.definitionFit: Roget's work, a book of synonyms, is a classic reference book.

clue.text: Being so stupid is by no means rare

definitions.meaning: thickly packed, the opposite of thin or rarefied

explanation.surface: Someone is told their foolishness is quite common.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense means thick-headed, and a dense gas or forest is thick, not rarefied.
